summary: PAPER-FU-24 is a careful and unusually deep extraction of Fu's Annals paper, and its seven source issues stand. I recomputed each of them, including E3's criterion (2λ(Δ)+1 a square in Z_p) and E7's norm bound. Theorems 1.2–1.5 stand, with Theorem 1.5 resting on AW14 as the extraction says. I read arXiv v2 in full (hash as recorded). I could not fetch the published NSF copy, so the new source issues are stated against v2, whose numbering the extraction collated with print. There are 17 findings: 7 medium and 10 low. Medium: (1) route 2's D(G), Fréchet–Stein and Frommer theory is also planned by LocallyAnalyticRepresentationsOfLocalGroups (DL17 route 3, Ding 25); (2) uniform groups, the Iwasawa series and finite global dimension now have NE.0 nodes, and the NE packet says they have no owner, while route 2 claims them; item 100 is still 'missing'; (3) route 3 re-plans ALS material: the boundary sequence (ALS.2/ALS.4), Poincaré–Lefschetz duality (ALS.5) and the Eichler–Shimura–Harder injection, which FIX-RT-AREA-iwasawa-1 /34 also requested from ALS.5; (4) Ore's theorem for noetherian domains is in pinned Mathlib; (6) no item defines G-homology H_i(G, M ⊗ W) of Iwasawa modules; (11) E1–E7 are recorded twice, in the errata file and the result, with conflicting kind and affects, so the register shows 14 entries; (14) banach-iwasawa-duality duplicates the ST02a sub-stage proposed by FIX-RT-AREA-automorphic-1 /17. Low: uncited Tau Ceti PBW spanning and glCasimir; the homology-to-cohomology step of §7; Harish-Chandra and the triangular decomposition planned only over algebraically closed fields; Tau Ceti ProfiniteProPGroups L9 completedGroupAlgebra not cited; CC.6 plans only cohomological descent; sourceVersions missing (the errata file fails check_errata); a false independence statement in REV-ERRATA; and three unrecorded gaps in the paper (Theorem 4.2's real radii against ST03 4.5(ii), Theorem 3.2's low-coordinate strips, and §7's reduction to K_f = GK^p). Disclosure: this session wrote FIX-RT-AREA-automorphic-1 (NE.0 widening, CC and PMIA stages) and FIX-RT-AREA-iwasawa-1. Findings 2, 3 and 14 touch proposals from those reports, and each fix names both sides.

Disclosure. This session wrote FIX-RT-AREA-automorphic-1 and FIX-RT-AREA-iwasawa-1. Three findings touch them. Finding 2: automorphic-1 /3 widened NE.0 and requested an Auslander-regularity node, but left the ownership gap for uniform groups open. Finding 14: automorphic-1 /17 proposes PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L1:banach-representations, which duplicates banach-iwasawa-duality. Source, preprint. arXiv:2201.11190v2 (15 February 2024), https://arxiv.org/pdf/2201.11190v2, fetched 30 September 2026. 25 pages, SHA-256 d71e9d3f8d3a1217743c3ba72c9a9630981f054ecefd943ff4edb4879b842614, the same as the extraction's. Read in full, §§1–7 and the references, through pdftotext. The arXiv listing shows v1 (26 January 2022) and v2 (15 February 2024) only.

Source, version of record. Ann. of Math. 200 (2024), no. 1, 123–152, doi:10.4007/annals.2024.200.1.3. The NSF PAR copy https://par.nsf.gov/servlets/purl/10625156 could not be fetched on 30 September 2026 (the connection timed out after 136 s, twice), and the conventional Annals PDF paths return 404. The Annals article page (received 2 February 2022, revised 21 December 2023, accepted 9 February 2024, published online 3 July 2024) links no erratum, and Crossref's record has no update-to, updated-by or relation entry. My quotations are therefore from arXiv v2. The extraction and the review both report that the published numbered statements agree with v2, the only addition being 'Suppose K_f is sufficiently small' in Corollary 1.3, so findings 15–17 are stated against v2 and should be re-checked against the published pages.

Auxiliary source. Schneider–Teitelbaum, Algebras of p-adic distributions and admissible representations, arXiv math/0206056v1 (SHA-256 e8a60a25f246692b048789235fb8efaf6d44ae65fdbb7cc738c8caeae67efcd5, equal to the extraction's ST03-v1), §4, Theorem 4.5 and Remark 4.6, read for finding 15.

All 137 items (12 library, 11 planned, 114 missing), the 6 routes with their briefs, the prerequisites, coverage, inspection and continuation records, and all 7 sourceIssues with their review verdicts. Every missing item is routed exactly once: 38 + 49 + 25 + 4 + 1 + 1 = 118 route slots, 114 missing plus the 4 planned items in route 4. The route graph (route 1 → 2 → 3, and source routes into CC, NE.0 and PMIA L1) has no cycle.

Source issues recomputed. E1: with N_j = z_j A + z̄_j B for a Z-basis (z_1, z_2) of the cusp lattice, the Koszul complex of the commuting nilpotents A, B on Sym^n ⊗ Sym^n-bar has cohomology (1,2,1), so |dim H^i_c − dim H^i| ≤ 3c for i = 1, 2. E2: c_0 against ℓ^∞. E3: with Fu's normalization dχ(h) = μ ∈ Z_p arbitrary, λ(Δ) = ½μ² ± μ (or ½μ² − ½ after the ρ-shift), so the induced set is {2λ(Δ)+1 a square in Z_p}. That set is exactly the closure of {½k(k+2)}, which confirms E3's claim that Theorem 1.4 needs genericity only there, and 3 is not a 3-adic square. E4: p^a ∈ m^{ea} ⊆ m^{a+1} for e ≥ 2 and a ≥ 1. E5: r_1 = p^{−1/p} > p^{−1/(p−1)}, outside the proved small-radius range. E6: r = r_1 + 2r_2 against r_1 + r_2 entries. E7: at r = p^{−2/3}, ‖log(1+H)‖_r = p^{−2/3}, so ‖h‖_r = p^{1/3} and ‖Δ‖_r ≤ p^{2/3} < p = |p^{−1}|. All seven stand.

Fu's own computations re-checked. The Casimir eigenvalue ½k(k+2), and Prop. 3.4's λ_k = ¼k(k+2) as the scalar of ef. Lemma 3.3's count Σ_c = (d+1)². Theorem 3.2's majorant 2Σα_i∏_{j≠i}(k_j+1). The dimension (n+1)² of the §6 graded pieces of the algebraic functions. Prop. 5.3's ‖X_i‖_{r_n} = p^{n−1}, consistent with PAPER-DOSPINESCU-LEBRAS-17/E11. The i = 0 and i = 1 cases of Theorem 1.4's proof. Prop. 3.4's integral claim, tested by exact integer lattice computation for Sym^n Z², n ≤ 7: the Z-span of the images of PBW monomials of degree ≤ n equals that of all monomials of degree ≤ 3n+4 up to an index that is a power of 2, so nothing fails at p = 3, 5, 7. The continuation's bounded-division identity for M_{a,b,c}(Δ − λ), re-derived by hand.

findings.claim: The item treats Ore's theorem for noetherian domains as outside the libraries ('The noetherian-domain Ore theorem … not claimed to follow from the mere carrier'), and the whole item is 'missing'. Pinned Mathlib has it. A nontrivial left-noetherian ring satisfies the strong rank condition. A domain with the strong rank condition has its nonzero divisors as a left Ore set. Then R[R⁰⁻¹] is a division ring. So the classical left division ring of fractions of a left-noetherian domain, which is Definition 2.1's L for a left module, is library. What is missing is the right-handed version (via the opposite ring), flatness of the Ore localisation on both sides (no flatness statement exists in the OreLocalization files), and the rank API.

A search of Mathlib/RingTheory/OreLocalization/*.lean for 'Flat' finds nothing. Fu arXiv v2 Def. 2.1, p. 5: 'The field of fractions L of A is a division ring that is flat over A on both sides.'

findings.claim: Two halves of what these items need are already in pinned Tau Ceti, and no item cites them. Tau Ceti f790474 has the spanning half of PBW over any commutative ring for a linearly ordered spanning family: the ordered monomials of length ≤ k span the k-th PBW filtration step. It also proves that Sym_R(L) → gr U_R(L) is surjective, and reduces injectivity to a degreewise statement. The extraction cites only the filtration and the graded pieces, and says 'no ordered-monomial independence is inferred'. So free-lie-pbw and integral-sl2-pbw overstate what is missing: only linear independence is. For integral-central-generators: Tau Ceti has the central trace-form Casimir element of U(gl_n) over any commutative ring. For n = 2 and 2 invertible, Fu's Δ = ½h² + ef + fe equals Ω − ½z² with z = E11 + E22 central. So centrality of Δ follows from the library element through U(gl_2) = U(sl_2) ⊗ R[z].
